pairs.why: Both trains have the same smooth, semi-glossy black metal with small rivets and rods, so surface finish gives no reason to choose.
B's posts and planks are smoother with only small nail heads, like the real cards' quiet wood, while A's posts carry bigger decorative grain.
B's sole dots are fewer and larger and sit on a smooth surface like the real sandals, while A's dense fine dot field reads as busier texture.
A has stitched seams and panel edges as fine detail, like the preferred saddles, while B is one smooth, slightly lacquered form.
A's glass is thick and soft with a chunky base and simple highlights like the real glass, while B is thinner and more finely rendered.
A's soft satin plastic has gentle highlights, like the real player, while B's body is more glossy with hotter, sharper highlights.
A's fins are smooth with a soft gloss like the real rubber, while B adds ribbed grooves and scratchy marks on the blades, which makes it too texture-y.
Both show similar soft plush fur, glossy wood and small bolt details, so finish gives no clear reason to choose.
